In the morning, the ship sails through the Murray Channel between Navarino and Hoste islands.

The first stop is historic Wulaia Bay.

Charles Darwin and Captain FitzRoy described this area during the voyage of the Beagle in the 1830s.

After visiting the museum in the former radio station, you can choose from three walking routes of varying difficulty.

Each leads through Magellanic forest to a lookout over the bay.

Before you sail, you can leave a letter or postcard in the wooden postbox for future travellers, carrying on an old maritime tradition.

In the afternoon, the ship crosses Nassau Bay towards a remote archipelago.

The main stop is Cape Horn National Park.

Landing on the island is possible only when weather and sea conditions permit.

A Dutch expedition discovered Cape Horn in 1616 and named it after Hoorn in West Friesland.

The rocky headland rises 425 metres.

For many years, this area was the only sea route between the Pacific and Atlantic oceans.

The park was designated a UNESCO World Biosphere Reserve in 2005.

The Chilean Navy operates a permanent lighthouse on the island.
Wooded islands and mountainous shores at Wulaia Bay, Chile
Wulaia Bay: blue water and green shores seen through the branches
30 December: Ushuaia and Tierra del Fuego

Arrive in Ushuaia at approximately 08:30.

The city has a population of about 45,000.

After disembarking, you’ll tour Tierra del Fuego National Park.

The park covers more than 63,000 hectares and has around 6 km of coastline along the Beagle Channel.

Beavers, albatrosses and penguins are found in the park.

The route takes in the Pipo River, Mount Susana, Ensenada Bay, Redonda Island, Lake Roca and Lapataia Bay.

You can also see lagoons, beaver dams and areas of forest.

The Tren del Fin del Mundo, or Train at the End of the World, runs through the park.

Its locomotives are styled after narrow-gauge trains from the early 20th century.

The train stops at Macarena station, where there is a museum settlement dedicated to the Yámana people and a small waterfall.

After the excursion, check in to a Valley View Room at Arakur Hotel.
